# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Note the date, time, and location of the water-quality test.
3. Identify the municipal water facility being tested – this could be a specific treatment plant, water distribution system, or sampling point.
4. List the parameters that were tested, e.g., bacteria levels, chlorine levels, lead, pH, turbidity, etc.
5. Document any failures or exceedances of public health and safety standards.
6. Record the concentrations of contaminants that exceeded regulatory limits.
7. Include the name of the testing laboratory or entity that conducted the analysis.
8. Take note of any follow-up actions recommended by the laboratory or health officials.
9. Consult with the municipal department or water authority for any official communication they may issue.
10. Verify the accuracy of your information before reporting.
11. Include references to applicable laws and regulations guiding permissible contaminant levels.
12. Clarify whether the water sample was a routine test or a response to a specific incident.
13
